nodes.summary: For subgroups $F$ and $H$ of a group $G$, $G$ is a Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and complement $H$ (Kourovka 6.53) if $G = F \rtimes H$ (that is, $F$ is normal in $G$, $F \cap H = 1$ and $FH = G$), $F \ne 1$, $H \ne 1$, $H \cap gHg^{-1} = 1$ for every $g \in G \setminus H$, and the non-trivial elements of $F$ are exactly the elements of $G$ that lie in no conjugate $gHg^{-1}$ of $H$.
nodes.title: Frobenius group with given kernel and complement

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group in which every element has finite order, and let $A$ be a normal abelian subgroup of $G$ that is neither trivial nor all of $G$ and such that for every $a \in A$ with $a \ne 1$ the centralizer $C_G(a)$ of $a$ in $G$ is contained in $A$. Then there are subgroups $F$ and $H$ of $G$ such that $G$ is a Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and complement $H$. This answers Kourovka Problem 20.96 (A. I.…
nodes.title: Lytkina–Mazurov theorem on periodic Frobenius groups

nodes.summary: The statement, posed by A. I. Sozutov, that for every group $G$ in which every element has finite order and every normal abelian subgroup $A$ of $G$ that is neither trivial nor all of $G$ and such that for every $a \in A$ with $a \ne 1$ the centralizer $C_G(a)$ of $a$ in $G$ is contained in $A$, there are subgroups $F$ and $H$ of $G$ such that $G$ is a Frobenius group with kernel $F$ and complement $H$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 20.96 (periodic Frobenius groups)
